preamble: The solution to 1 across is normal. All the other across solutions must be modified as per 1 across before entry in the grid. These entries are not real words. Both the word play in these clues and their letter counts relate to the required entries. All the down solutions are normal.

clue.text: What you must do to make former partner go? Quite the opposite!

definitions.text: What you must do to make former partner go? Quite the opposite!

parts.words: What you must do to make former partner go
parts.note: the former partner is an ex; to turn ex into a word meaning go, you would have to add the little word it
reverses the instruction: instead of adding that little word, you drop it

explanation.surface: Advice on getting rid of an ex, with a teasing twist at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: EX plus IT makes EXIT, so adding IT is what makes the ex go; the opposite is LEAVE IT OUT. That phrase is also the theme: every other across answer drops IT before entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a literal instruction to omit a word, and also British slang for 'stop that!'

clue.text: Delicacy shown by family member taking a step back in the first place

indicators.text: taking a step back in the first place
indicators.note: the opening letter moves back one place in the alphabet

parts.note: a mobster belongs to a crime family

explanation.surface: A relative stepping back out of tactfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: Family member means a Mafia family, not a relative. Stepping M back one place in the alphabet gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobster is a prized and expensive seafood, a classic gourmet treat.

clue.text: Workforce repeatedly accepts board's conclusion, then stops at reform

indicators.note: the built group plugs the gap in at, as a stopper fills a hole

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the workforce takes the letter in among its own

parts.note: men are the workforce, and repeatedly asks for the word twice

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Staff keep agreeing to the board's decision, then halt at reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to improve a law or document.

clue.text: Impossible odds? Yes and no

parts.note: numbers that cannot be odd, and also a betting price
they are odds in betting, but not odd numbers

explanation.walkthrough: Even numbers can never be odd, yet a bet at even money is quoted at odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is the betting price where the stake is matched one for one.

clue.text: Result of periodic fluctuations in current and supply from the mains

definitions.text: Result of periodic fluctuations in current
definitions.meaning: first meaning: water brought in by the rise and fall of the tides
second meaning: water from the main, the old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as electricity and plumbing; the mains is the sea, and the fluctuations are tides.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidewater is water carried by the tide, and coastal land reached by it.

clue.text: Perhaps John's content hearing solver is at home

indicators.note: what you hear is the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: the solver is you, and at home is in: you're in

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a man named John is happy while the solver stays home.
explanation.walkthrough: John is US slang for a toilet, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Urine is what fills a toilet bowl, so it is an example of the lavatory's contents.

clue.text: Take no part in guide to strip clubs

indicators.note: stripping something away removes it, so the clubs letter is taken out of the guide

parts.note: a scout guides others, going ahead to find the way

explanation.surface: A tourist guidebook advising readers to avoid strip clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives SIT OUT; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the shortened entry SOUT. C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit out a dance or game is to abstain from it rather than join in.

clue.text: Dishonour of political leader's departure from platform

indicators.note: the letter leaves the word for platform

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disgraced politician stepping down from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is the shame and public hatred attaching to someone, a synonym for disgrace.

clue.text: Occupation hollowed out the French town

indicators.note: with the middle scooped out, only the outer letters remain

parts.note: taken as written
Nancy is a city in Lorraine, north-east France

explanation.surface: A French town emptied out by an invading army.
explanation.walkthrough: Occupation looks military or professional, but means living in a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the holding of a property as tenant, i.e. residing in it.

clue.text: Employees' pay rise is reviewed and, unfortunately, overturned

indicators.note: turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret

indicators.note: looked at afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Staff are dismayed when a promised pay rise is reconsidered and reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: Pay rise looks like one phrase; pay belongs to the definition, and rise is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaries are the fixed regular payments made to staff.

clue.text: Time in drunken bender, after which one cannot go on

definitions.text: after which one cannot go on

indicators.note: the time letter sits within the jumbled letters
a drunken thing reels about, so the letters of bender are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinking binge so heavy that the drinker has to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives BITTER END; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry BTEREND.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on to the bitter end means persisting until the final limit, beyond which there is nothing more.

clue.text: Artificial life wants a new beginning

indicators.note: to want is to lack, so these letters are missing from the word for life

parts.note: animation is liveliness, the state of being alive and spirited
taken as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of new is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A synthetic existence that needs a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives IMITATION; the theme drops IT, and ANIMATION without its opening A and N gives the entry IMATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a copy made to look like the genuine article, so it is fake or synthetic.

clue.text: Juicy items in American tabloids circulated without any legal objections, initially

indicators.note: papers circulate, but letters sent round in a circle come out rearranged
without here means lacking, so these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of these words is taken

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gossip in US tabloids spread freely because no lawyer objected.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives TIDBITS, the American spelling of titbits; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry TIDBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidbits are small tasty morsels, and by extension choice pieces of gossip or news.

clue.text: One's said to drive badly while drinking case of vodka with husband

indicators.note: a drinker takes something in, so the vodka's outer letters go inside

parts.note: while and when both mean at the time that

indicators.note: the case is the outside, so only the first and last letters are used

parts.note: taken as written
a husband is a woman's man

explanation.surface: A driver who has drunk vodka with her husband is a menace on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives WHITE VAN MAN, the British stereotype of the aggressive delivery-van driver; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds WHEVANMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock British caricature of a reckless, discourteous tradesman behind the wheel.

clue.text: Repeating tedious speech always disrupts

indicators.note: something that disrupts breaks into the middle, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a rant is a long, tiresome tirade
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Someone droning on, always interrupting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives REITERANT; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry REERANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiterant describes something said or done again and again, an adjective from reiterate.

clue.text: Articles about Jersey soldier's defence

indicators.note: the two articles go around the rest

parts.note: two indefinite articles, a and a
a polo shirt is a kind of jersey
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Items of uniform worn by a soldier for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a garment here, not the Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written justification of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: Wife experiencing thrilling feeling on purpose

parts.note: a thrill makes the skin tingle, so someone feeling one is tingly

explanation.surface: A wife who gets her thrills deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives WITTINGLY; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry WTINGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something wittingly means doing it knowingly and intentionally, not by accident.

clue.text: Any cuts essentially must follow source of consumer advice

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: Which? is the British consumer magazine that tests products

indicators.note: the essence is the inside, so the outer letters go

parts.note: severs means cuts

explanation.surface: Any spending cuts must heed the consumer watchdog's advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Whichever means any one at all, whatever the choice.

clue.text: Irregular ultimately swaps sides and becomes … irregular!

indicators.note: the altered letters turn into something new, in a fresh order
the final letter of the first word changes from the right-hand letter to the left-hand one

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A paradox: an irregular thing changes sides and ends up irregular anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: R is right and L is left, so the last R turns to L. A guerrilla is an irregular soldier, so the second irregular is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla fighter belongs to an unofficial force rather than a regular army.

clue.text: Cake found in middle of floor covered in dog hair?

indicators.note: the fur surrounds the middle letter, as a floor would be covered

parts.note: the question mark flags an example: a dog is a pet, and its hair is fur

indicators.note: the centre letter of the word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cake dropped on the floor and now coated in the dog's hairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives PETIT FOUR, a small fancy cake; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry PETFOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit four is a bite-sized iced fancy served with coffee, a kind of small cake.

clue.text: Bookmaker's runner scratching either second or first place

indicators.note: a scratched runner is withdrawn, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a sprinter is a fast runner
S abbreviates second, and here is also the word's first letter

explanation.surface: A racing bookie's horse withdrawn while placed first or second.
explanation.walkthrough: Bookmaker suggests a bookie, but means one who makes books.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer produces books, so is literally their maker.

clue.text: Uncertainty surrounds partners' games, love notwithstanding

indicators.note: the doubt word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: an if is a doubt, as in no ifs or buts
North and South are partners at the bridge table
PE is physical education, school games

explanation.surface: Doubt hangs over a couple's sporting matches, despite their affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives IN SPITE OF; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry INSPEOF. Love is zero in tennis scoring, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean despite, introducing something that does not prevent what follows.

clue.text: Limp holding up detective missing end part of leg

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means read from the bottom, so backwards
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a dick is slang for a private detective
the calf is the back of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A limping man supports a detective who has injured his leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Limp looks like a verb for walking lamely; it is the adjective meaning floppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaccid means soft and slack, lacking firmness.

clue.text: Popular kind of maths cut the odds, honestly!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular, as in the in thing
kind and good both mean benevolent

indicators.note: removing the odd-numbered letters leaves the even ones

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that a fashionable branch of maths really did reduce the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives IN GOOD FAITH; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds INGOODFAH. 'Kind of maths' looks like one phrase, but kind is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in good faith means acting sincerely and without deceit.

clue.text: Singer's requirement for perfect pitch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informer, who sings to the police
second meaning: the turf a playing field needs

explanation.walkthrough: Perfect pitch sounds musical, matching singer; here it is a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for a police informer, and the turf covering a playing field.

clue.text: Ballet movement to start with third position transferring to fifth

indicators.note: the third letter moves to the fifth slot

parts.note: to found is to start up, as a company

explanation.surface: A dancer beginning in third position then moving to fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: Third and fifth position are real ballet stances, but here they are letter places.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondu is a ballet step in which the supporting leg bends to lower the body.

clue.text: Fall, ignoring the boundaries of headland

parts.note: to err is to fall into error

indicators.note: the outer letters are left off, so only the inside of the word counts

parts.note: the word is split in two: head, as in Beachy Head, is the wordplay, and land is the definition

explanation.surface: A climber falling, having missed the edges of a clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: Headland splits into head and land: land is the definition. It gives ERITREA; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry ERREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country on the Red Sea coast of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Studying part of the Odyssey in Greek

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Odyssey and into in Greek

explanation.surface: Reading a passage of Homer's epic in the original language.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something means looking at it closely; eying is a variant spelling.

clue.text: It's established practice to have something charged on incomplete transactions

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: trade is buying and selling, commercial transactions
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: It is customary to pay commission on deals that fall through.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives TRADITION; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry TRADION.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom handed down over generations and long observed.

clue.text: Surprisingly civil or horribly bitter?

indicators.note: a surprising result is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone's manner is unexpectedly polite or dreadfully harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives VITRIOLIC; the theme drops IT, and the anagram builds the entry VRIOLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic means savagely caustic, from vitriol, the corrosive sulphuric acid.

clue.text: Attempts to get better result in crowd quietly melting away

indicators.note: something that melts away disappears, so this letter is removed

parts.note: a press is a crowd pressing together

explanation.surface: Trying to improve a result while the crowd silently drifts off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives RESITS, British for exams taken again; the theme drops IT, and the wordplay builds the entry RESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Resits are second sittings of failed exams, taken in the hope of a better mark.

clue.text: Hormone factory is winding up angry lad

indicators.note: winding twists, so these letters are wound into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hormones are what's winding up a furious teenage boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives PITUITARY GLAND; the theme drops both ITs, and the anagram builds the entry PUARYGLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The pituitary gland at the base of the brain secretes hormones controlling growth and other glands.
